cards.explanation: The answer is to come and heal his servant. The centurion, an army officer, hears about Jesus and sends Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant (Luke 7:3). His servant is sick and about to die. I think when somebody you care about is that sick, you go to the One who can help.

The reason the elders give is that he loves their nation and built their synagogue. They say, "…he loves our nation and has built our synagogue." (Luke 7:5) Love for the people and a building to show for it. That's a reason you can point at, friends, and the elders plead earnestly with Jesus about it (Luke 7:4).

The answer is False. The centurion's message says, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof." (Luke 7:6) There's no "hurry inside" anywhere in it, friends. He calls Jesus "Lord" and says he's not worthy to have Him come under his roof.

He asks Jesus by just saying the word. The centurion says, "But just say the word, and my servant will be healed." (Luke 7:7) No house call needed. He believes a word from Jesus is enough, and that's a whole lot of trust packed into one sentence, friends.

The answer is False. The centurion says, "I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes." (Luke 7:8) He says they go and they come, and he never mentions an argument. His whole point, friends, is that when the word is given, the thing happens.

The word is "marvels." The text says, "When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion." (Luke 7:9) Jesus heard those words about authority and was amazed. Then He turns to the crowd and says, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith." (Luke 7:9)

Jesus says He hasn't found faith this great even in Israel. He turns to the crowd and says, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith." (Luke 7:9) The man trusted that a word from Jesus was enough, friends. The centurion is a Roman army officer, and Jesus says this in front of everyone.

The answer is True. The text says, "…when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health." (Luke 7:10) The servant who was about to die is well. The centurion asked for a word, friends, and when the messengers got home, there he was, healthy.
